speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You presented with neck and arm pain, paresthesias, and muscle weakness. To understand the cause, can you tell me if the pain radiates from your neck specifically down into your arm or hand?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of burning pain in his neck and arms, accompanying paresthesias in his hands. Over the past 3 months, he has experienced increasing weakness in both hands. He has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and hypertension. He was involved in a motor vehicle accident 3 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Cervical Spondylotic Myelopathy / Cervical Stenosis with Radiculopathy.

The patient's history of one-sided or bilateral upper extremity weakness, paresthesias, and pain radiating from the neck, combined with his age and long-standing diabetes, strongly points to cervical spine pathology. While the diabetes and past trauma are relevant, the specific pattern of neurological decline suggests nerve root or spinal cord compression.

I have made a diagnosis based on the clinical presentation and history provided. No further tests are required at this moment to establish the working diagnosis of cervical spondylosis with myelopathy or radiculopathy.
